options.summary: Claim that Co-Pilot AI Scientist v3 improves paper quality and outperforms autonomous AI Scientist-v2.
evidence: No expert or rubric-based paper-quality score yet
No broad matched multi-task autonomous versus full co-pilot benchmark yet
Two matched Causality pairs are mixed
risks: Contradicted by Pair 2 and by the two-pair mean favoring autonomous on test MAE.

options.summary: Claim a modular co-pilot architecture with pilot evidence for feasible human gates, OpenEvolve-style subproblem search, evaluator-gate failure handling, and mixed matched-budget results.
risks: Still below top-conference evidence bar without broader matched comparisons.

human_decision: Use pilot_architecture_claim; demote strong_superiority_claim to future work.
rationale: The evidence supports a reproducible architecture and several narrow feasibility claims, but does not support a broad superiority claim. The manuscript should be conservative and explicit about remaining evidence requirements.

allowed_claims: OpenEvolve-style search can help some machine-gradeable subproblems
program search should be gated rather than automatic
evaluator gates should reject non-executable and metric-gaming branches
blocked_claims: full co-pilot v3 outperforms autonomous AI Scientist-v2

follow_up_checks: Run more matched autonomous versus human-gated comparisons across tasks and seeds.
Add expert or rubric-based paper-quality scores.
Run one complete online four-loop trajectory with all gates active before upgrading the central claim.
